title: TechCrunch Mobility: AV companies pick their lanes
summary:
### **Core Story / Main Event**
The article analyzes the current state of the autonomous vehicle (AV) industry, focusing on the transition from testing to commercialization. It highlights three primary scaling strategies: partnerships, geographic concentration, and user expansion, while also reporting on industry safety failures, IPO activity, and upcoming events at Disrupt 2026.

---

### **Important Names, Companies, and Key People**
*   **Companies:** Wayve, Mercedes-Benz, Nissan, Stellantis, Uber, Waymo, Aurora, Zoox, Carro, Spinny, PMI Electro Mobility Solutions, Eco Ceres, May Mobility, Ultraviolette, Comma, Einride, Nvidia, Pit Pro Automation, The Boring Company, Tesla, Volkswagen, MOIA America, Beep, Mobileye, Rivian, Also, Mind Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, GM, Waabi.
*   **Key People:** 
    *   **Kirsten Korosec:** TechCrunch Transportation Editor.
    *   **Chris Urmson:** CEO of Aurora.
    *   **Sean O’Kane:** TechCrunch Senior Reporter.
    *   **George Hotz:** Founder of Comma.
    *   **Elon Musk:** Founder of The Boring Company and CEO of Tesla.
    *   **Bryan Reimer:** MIT Researcher.
    *   **RJ Scaringe:** CEO of Rivian.
    *   **Lip-Bu Tan:** Intel CEO (Adviser to Ultraviolette).
    *   **Les Karpas:** Nvidia’s head of physical AI.
    *   **Mark Wahlberg:** Disrupt 2026 speaker.

---

### **Detailed Breakdown of Companies, Products, and Features**

**AV Scaling Strategies & Implementations**
*   **Wayve**
    *   **Mercedes-Benz Partnership:** Integrating automated driving tech into at least one model within the next two years.
    *   **Product Spec:** Level 2 (handles certain maneuvers; requires engaged human driver).
    *   **Other Partners:** Nissan and Stellantis.
    *   **Robotaxi Venture:** Partnership with Nissan and Uber to launch a robotaxi service in Tokyo.
*   **Waymo**
    *   **Fleet Size:** Roughly 4,000 robotaxis.
    *   **Geographic Concentration:** ~80% of fleet located in California and Texas.
    *   **Growth Metric:** Texas fleet grew by more than 49% in the last three weeks.
    *   **Target Demographic:** Expanding user base to include teenagers.
*   **Aurora**
    *   **Focus:** Self-driving trucks; concentrated in Texas.
    *   **2024 Goal:** Plans for more than 200 driverless trucks by the end of the year.
    *   **2030 Goal:** Targeting more than 30,000 driverless trucks in operation.
*   **Zoox**
    *   **Incident:** Grounded test fleet in Atlanta due to safety driver exposure to gases (CO2, carbon monoxide, or hydrogen sulfide).
    *   **Vehicle Used:** Toyota Highlander SUVs equipped with Zoox self-driving systems.
    *   **Outcome:** OSHA inquiry opened following a worker complaint.
*   **The Boring Company**
    *   **Project:** "Simple precursor Hyperloop" between Austin and San Antonio.
    *   **Spec:** Aims to reduce travel time between cities to less than 30 minutes.
*   **Tesla**
    *   **Product:** All-electric Semi trucks (first deliveries now starting).
*   **Volkswagen / MOIA America**
    *   **ID Buzz:** Return to the U.S. is reportedly delayed.
    *   **MOIA America/Beep Partnership:** Launching passenger services in Lake Nona, Orlando, using self-driving ID Buzz vehicles equipped with Mobileye tech (includes human operator).

**Other Transportation & Tech Developments**
*   **Ultraviolette:** India-based electric motorcycle manufacturer; raised $85 million.
*   **Comma:** Aftermarket hands-off driver-assistance tech; currently under federal investigation following five crashes (three deaths).
*   **Einride:** Swedish autonomous/electric trucking; adopting Nvidia’s Hyperion platform for its next-gen self-driving system.
*   **Pit Pro Automation:** Developed a tire-changing robot; first deployment live in Canada.
*   **Rivian:** Developing R2, robotaxis, and automated driving; spinouts include "Also" and "Mind Robotics."

---

### **Financials, Pricing, and Dates**
*   **IPO Activity:**
    *   **Carro:** Considering dual listing on Nasdaq and Singapore Exchange.
    *   **Spinny & PMI Electro Mobility Solutions:** Filed confidentially for IPOs.
    *   **Eco Ceres:** Plans to raise ~$1 billion in a Hong Kong IPO.
    *   **May Mobility:** Planning to go public via merger with a blank-check company.
*   **Funding:** Ultraviolette raised $85 million.
*   **Disrupt 2026 Event:**
    *   **Dates:** October 13–15.
    *   **Ticket Offers:** 25% off (up to $200 savings) and 50% off a second ticket if purchased by Sept 25, 11:59 p.m. PT.
    *   **Discount Code:** `mobility30` for 30% off.

---

### **Direct Quotes**
*   **Chris Urmson (Aurora CEO):** Stated that Aurora has “emerged from the building stage.”
*   **Sean O’Kane (Insider Note):** “Customers will be able to take delivery of the truck whenever they are ready, though charging infrastructure remains a hurdle.”

title: How to use Android apps on your Windows PC (and why you might want to)
summary:
### Research Analysis: How to use Android apps on your Windows PC

**Core Story / Main Event**
The author explores the methods, tools, and motivations for running Android applications on a Windows PC. The narrative is driven by the author's desire to play the mobile game *Destiny: Rising* on a larger screen with better hardware performance (mouse/keyboard support and higher graphics) after the development of *Destiny 2* ended.

**Important Names, Companies, and Brands**
*   **Companies/Developers:** Google, Microsoft, Net Ease, Nvidia, Samsung.
*   **Key People:** Max Miller (Author/Engadget).
*   **Hardware/Brands:** Windows 11, Samsung Galaxy Tab S10 Ultra, Nvidia RTX 4070 Ti Super.

**Complete List of Products, Features, and Tools**
*   **Android Emulators (General)**
    *   **Functionality:** Creates virtual phones to run apps from the Play Store or other sources; allows "parallel instances" (running multiple emulated devices simultaneously).
    *   **Target Users:** Mobile gamers, content creators, developers, DIY tinkerers.
    *   **Hardware Requirement:** Generally compatible with any computer made in the past decade.
*   **BlueStacks**
    *   **Type:** Android Emulator.
    *   **Core Characteristic:** Described as a "legitimate app" but heavily cluttered with ads across the interface.
*   **Mu Mu Player**
    *   **Type:** Android Emulator.
    *   **Developer:** Net Ease.
    *   **Pricing:** Free.
    *   **Specifications:** Recently updated to Android 15.
    *   **Core Functionality:** Serves as a PC portal for Net Ease games; contains fewer ads than BlueStacks (primarily on loading screens).
*   **Google Play Games for PC**
    *   **Type:** Lightweight virtual machine project by Google.
    *   **Functionality:** Translates Android games directly to PC.
    *   **Limitation:** Only works with a select band of titles from developers who have opted in.
    *   **Supported Titles Mentioned:** *Genshin Impact*, *Clash of Clans*, *Disco Elysium*.
    *   **Unsupported Titles Mentioned:** *Destiny: Rising*.
*   **Windows Subsystem for Android**
    *   **Status:** Dropped/Discontinued in 2024.
    *   **Original Purpose:** Native Android app compatibility for Windows 11.
*   **Phone Link (Windows 11)**
    *   **Functionality:** Wireless casting of Android phone apps or screen to desktop.
    *   **Distinction:** Apps run on the phone hardware, not directly on the PC.

**Pricing, Dates, and Financials**
*   **Release/Timeline Dates:** 
    *   Windows Subsystem for Android dropped in 2024.
    *   Context provided for users looking for solutions in "2026 and beyond."
*   **Pricing:** Mu Mu Player is listed as "free."

**Use Cases for Emulation**
*   **Gaming:** Overcoming hardware caps (e.g., bypassing the 60 FPS cap on the Samsung Galaxy Tab S10 Ultra) and utilizing high-end GPUs (Nvidia RTX 4070 Ti Super).
*   **App Availability:** Accessing apps without PC editions (e.g., Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat, or specific smart-home/landlord apps).
*   **Development:** Testing apps for Android.
*   **Low-End Hardware:** Running slimmed-down Android versions of creative software on PCs that cannot handle pro-grade PC software.
*   **Workflow Management:** Siloing workflows or managing multiple accounts (farming in-game resources or separating work/personal accounts via parallel instances).

**Direct Quotes**
*   "Pretty much any computer made in the past decade can run an Android emulator, and as long as you're at least somewhat familiar with Android, you'll quickly get the hang of it."
*   "Bluestacks is a legitimate app, but it's chock full of ads that it seems to prioritize over all else, and they clutter up nearly every corner of the interface."
